correctness.rationale: Condition on the uniformly distributed oriented daughter size K=k (the two-colour Yule leaf-splitting urn), then the daughter subtrees are independent Yule trees. Cherry counts add; explicit small n=1,2,3,4 exceptions to known mu_m and second_m yield a_s={-1/3,1/3,0,...}, b_s={(-10n+3)/45,(10n+1)/45,-6/45,2/45,0,...}. For n>=10 the four extreme layers do not overlap. Averaging over the symmetric four k values gives unchanged n/3 and conditional variance 2(n+1)/45; unconditional variance is 2n/45. Independently propagated the cherry process by exact rational moment recurrences for n<=31 and checked 840 conditional/event equalities. No finite extrapolation supplies the all-n theorem.

evidence: Conditional independence in Markov-branching models plus known marginal moments mathematically permits deduction; no inspected primary statement gives this entire four-layer profile.

value.rationale: Root imbalance and cherry count are standard distinct tree shape observables. Their exact conditional relation has unexpected four-layer second-moment localization and exhibits a natural root-extremity event whose mean test is blind while variance shifts by a fixed 2/45. This supplies a motivated joint finite-sample statistic, despite derivation from known marginal moments; no efficacy theorem is claimed.

final_claim: For a Yule–Harding–Kingman tree of n>=10 leaves, the conditional cherry mean given oriented root daughter size k differs from n/3 only when min(k,n-k)=1,2, and the conditional raw second moment differs from n^2/9+2n/45 only for min(k,n-k)=1,2,3,4 with the stated exact deviations. Conditioning on at least one daughter of <=2 leaves keeps the mean n/3 but makes the variance 2(n+1)/45.
limitations: Only rooted YHK trees and n>=10, not PDA trees or all small n.
Finite moment propagation checks cannot establish all-n statements or historical uniqueness.
